issues.display_title: Issue #1810: [Style System] Clean up Editor shell and shared-style ownership
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Clarify ownership of the Virtual Gallery Editor shell and its genuinely shared styles while preserving the existing cascade.

In scope

  • Map every global Editor selector to its template/component consumers.
  • Keep only multi-consumer Editor shell patterns global, scoped below a unique Editor root.
  • Move one-feature selectors to their Angular component owners.
  • Remove or narrow duplicate overrides only after consumer and cascade analysis.
  • Audit existing ViewEncapsulation.None; migrate one component at a time when safe, otherwise scope every rule under its feature root.
  • Document remaining cross-component dependencies.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not combine large selector moves with Geist migration.
  • Do not delete compatibility CSS until visual and consumer checks prove it dead.
  • Do not add generic ::ng-deep rules.

Acceptance criteria

  • Each migrated selector has one clear owner.
  • Global Editor CSS contains only shared shell behavior with explicit consumers.
  • Any remaining ViewEncapsulation.None is justified and uniquely scoped.

Dependencies and order

Depends on Editor Bootstrap-independence issues. Precedes feature/dialog body migrations.

Verification

  • Run rg consumer searches for every moved/deleted selector.
  • Run focused component tests, pnpm test:styles, and the required Angular build.
  • Compare exact desktop/mobile screenshots and interactive shell states.

issues.display_title: Issue #1811: [Style System] Migrate Images and Edit Frame styles and dialogs
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Apply the new ownership model to the Editor Images/Add Artwork and Edit Frame areas, including feature-specific PrimeNG dialog content.

In scope

  • Move feature layout, cards, icons, fields, actions, tabs, and responsive rules to the owning components.
  • Keep reusable PrimeNG shell behavior global under src/assets/scss/primeNg/dialog/.
  • Use shared .v-dialog and mask patterns plus unique feature dialog classes.
  • Keep dialog body/content styling component-owned, using scoped :host ::ng-deep only where overlay rendering requires it.
  • Remove proven-dead legacy selectors and duplicate overrides.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not recreate src/assets/scss/primeNg/_dialog.scss.
  • Keep dialog/_index.scss import-only.
  • Do not put feature-only dialog body rules in global SCSS.
  • Preserve geometry, responsive behavior, interaction states, and user-content fonts.

Acceptance criteria

  • Images/Add Artwork and Edit Frame styles have clear component/global ownership.
  • No generic feature dialog selector leaks globally.
  • Removed selectors have no remaining consumers.

Dependencies and order

Depends on Editor shell ownership cleanup and Editor tab migration.

Verification

  • Search moved/deleted selectors across templates, TypeScript, and SCSS.
  • Review open/closed dialogs, masks, focus, errors, loading, tabs, desktop, and mobile.
  • Run focused tests and pnpm test:styles.
  • Follow AGENTS.md: use pnpm ng build --configuration=development if port 4200 is active; otherwise pnpm build:dev:ssr.

issues.display_title: Issue #1812: [Style System] Migrate General, Objects, and Text styles and dialogs
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Apply component ownership, token usage, and dialog boundaries to the Editor General, Objects, and Text feature areas.

In scope

  • Move feature-only layouts, controls, cards, lists, states, and responsive rules beside their owning components.
  • Retain only proven shared Editor-shell patterns globally.
  • Use shared PrimeNG dialog shells plus unique feature dialog wrappers.
  • Move dialog body/content styles to components and scope overlay penetration through the unique wrapper.
  • Remove dead legacy selectors after consumer/cascade verification.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not alter the Text/content font catalogue, its weights/styles, previews, or rendered gallery output.
  • Do not perform the Editor Geist batch here.
  • No generic global .confirm-dialog or equivalent body selector.

Acceptance criteria

  • General, Objects, and Text selectors each have a clear owner.
  • Feature dialog bodies are local and shared shell rules remain centralized.
  • User-authored typography remains byte-for-byte equivalent in mappings and visually equivalent in output.

Dependencies and order

Depends on Editor shell ownership cleanup and font-domain separation. Can follow the Images/Edit Frame pattern.

Verification

  • Search every moved/deleted selector and font mapping.
  • Review selection, add/edit/delete, validation, focus, dialog, empty/loading/error, desktop, and mobile states.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the AGENTS.md-required Angular build.

issues.display_title: Issue #1813: [Style System] Migrate Publish and Splash Screen styles and dialogs
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Complete feature ownership cleanup for the Editor Publish and Splash Screen flows while retaining their current UI and overlay behavior.

In scope

  • Move feature-specific layouts, previews, fields, actions, progress/status states, and responsive rules to their owners.
  • Reuse global .v-dialog/mask shell behavior and unique Publish/Splash feature wrappers.
  • Keep dialog bodies, icons, cards, and action layouts component-owned.
  • Remove dead duplicated or legacy selectors only after proving they have no consumers.
  • Narrow ::ng-deep and ViewEncapsulation.None usage where safely possible.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No workflow, upload, publishing, or preview behavior change.
  • No generic dialog body styles in global PrimeNG SCSS.
  • No Geist migration in this batch.

Acceptance criteria

  • Publish and Splash Screen styles have unambiguous ownership.
  • Overlay styling follows the repository dialog contract.
  • Loading, success, error, disabled, and responsive presentation matches the baseline.

Dependencies and order

Depends on Editor shell cleanup and the shared dialog pattern demonstrated by preceding feature batches.

Verification

  • Search moved/deleted selectors across source.
  • Exercise dialogs, masks, upload/progress, validation, success/error, and mobile states.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the AGENTS.md-required Angular build.
  • Compare exact baseline screenshots.

issues.display_title: Issue #1814: [Style System] Adopt Geist in Editor UI and verify legacy cleanup
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Finish the Editor pilot by moving product UI typography to Geist/Geist Mono in an isolated, reviewable batch, then deleting only legacy style code proven redundant.

In scope

  • Apply Geist to Editor product UI controls, labels, headings, panels, and overlays.
  • Apply Geist Mono only to documented technical values such as coordinates, dimensions, transforms, identifiers, and code/embed snippets.
  • Correct wrapping, truncation, alignment, or overflow exposed by new font metrics without redesigning geometry.
  • Audit and remove legacy UI font declarations, dead selectors, duplicate overrides, and obsolete compatibility rules in the Editor scope.
  • Record before/after CSS metrics and any intentional font-rendering differences.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • The user-content font catalogue, weights, styles, previews, and rendered gallery content must remain unchanged.
  • Prices, dates, body copy, and ordinary labels remain Geist, not Mono.
  • Do not delete a selector without consumer search, build, visual comparison, and state review.

Acceptance criteria

  • Editor product UI consistently uses Geist; Mono usage is limited to approved technical surfaces.
  • All Editor baseline states remain compositionally compatible.
  • Every deletion has evidence that it is unconsumed or redundant.
  • No Bootstrap dependency remains inside the Editor pilot scope.

Dependencies and order

Depends on all Editor foundation, Bootstrap-independence, ownership, and feature migration issues.

Verification

  • Run font/selector/Bootstrap searches, focused tests, and pnpm test:styles.
  • Run the required Angular build.
  • Review desktop/mobile, supported themes, all interaction states, and at least two content fonts.
  • Treat unexplained visual differences as failures.

issues.display_title: Issue #1815: [Style System] Consolidate shared buttons, fields, states, and native controls
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Promote the proven Editor control patterns into maintainable application-wide primitives while improving accessible state handling.

In scope

  • Consolidate shared button, field, label, validation, focus-visible, loading, disabled, empty, and error behavior.
  • Introduce component tokens only where multiple features share a stable contract.
  • Replace global native checkbox/radio hiding with explicit, scoped custom-control patterns.
  • Preserve useful APIs such as .btn and .form-control when app ownership is clearer than mass renaming.
  • Document variants, sizes, consumers, and extension rules.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not force visually different control sizes into one geometry.
  • Do not introduce a utility framework or speculative component library.
  • Feature-only variants remain local.

Acceptance criteria

  • Shared controls have complete base, focus, disabled, validation, and loading behavior.
  • Native controls are no longer hidden by an unscoped global selector.
  • New primitives have multiple real consumers and no Bootstrap implementation dependency.

Dependencies and order

Depends on the completed Editor pilot and token foundations. Required before broad feature slices.

Verification

  • Test keyboard focus, mouse/touch states, validation, disabled/loading, checkbox, and radio behavior.
  • Run focused tests, accessibility checks available in the repository, pnpm test:styles, and the required Angular build.
  • Compare representative application baselines.

issues.display_title: Issue #1816: [Style System] Refactor shared layout shell and PrimeNG dialog shells
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Establish clear global ownership for the application shell, navigation, and reusable PrimeNG dialog chrome before migrating feature slices.

In scope

  • Migrate header, footer, public layout, dashboard shell, and shared navigation styles to the new foundations.
  • Consolidate reusable .p-dialog, header, content, footer, .v-dialog, mask, and blur-mask behavior under src/assets/scss/primeNg/dialog/.
  • Keep dialog/_index.scss import-only and split shared behavior between appropriate partials.
  • Audit global overlays and document the unique-wrapper rule for component-owned bodies.
  • Remove only proven-dead shared-shell overrides.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not recreate src/assets/scss/primeNg/_dialog.scss.
  • Do not move feature-only dialog body styles into global SCSS.
  • Do not rely on generic selectors such as .confirm-dialog without a unique wrapper.
  • Preserve current layout and dialog geometry.

Acceptance criteria

  • Shared shell and reusable dialog chrome each have a single global owner.
  • Feature body styles remain with their components.
  • New dialogs can use styleClass="v-dialog feature-dialog" and shared mask classes without duplicating shell CSS.

Dependencies and order

Depends on token/shared-control foundations and the Editor dialog migration pattern. Precedes feature slices with dialogs.

Verification

  • Search for duplicate dialog-shell selectors and dead selectors.
  • Exercise representative headers/navigation and open/closed dialogs on desktop/mobile.
  • Run pnpm test:styles.
  • Follow AGENTS.md: use pnpm ng build --configuration=development if port 4200 is active; otherwise pnpm build:dev:ssr.

issues.display_title: Issue #1817: [Style System] Migrate Settings, Profile, and Account styles
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Apply the proven style architecture to Settings, Profile, and Account as the first non-Editor vertical slice.

In scope

  • Capture slice baselines and map global/component selector consumers.
  • Adopt tokens, Geist UI typography, shared controls, focus/state patterns, and shared dialog shells.
  • Move feature layouts and dialog bodies to their owners.
  • Replace active Bootstrap grid/utilities/mixins with component or proven shared CSS.
  • Remove legacy selectors and overrides only after cascade verification.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No feature, validation, responsive, or workflow redesign.
  • Feature-only dialog bodies stay local and use unique wrappers.
  • Do not remove Bootstrap globally.

Acceptance criteria

  • The slice follows global/component/overlay ownership rules.
  • It has no feature-level dependency on Bootstrap behavior.
  • Current desktop/mobile, themes, validation, and dialog presentation are preserved.

Dependencies and order

Depends on shared controls and shared layout/dialog shells. First Phase 4 slice.

Verification

  • Search migrated templates/SCSS for Bootstrap and deleted selectors.
  • Review forms, validation, save/delete confirmations, loading/error, keyboard focus, themes, and responsive states.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the AGENTS.md-required Angular build.

issues.display_title: Issue #1818: [Style System] Migrate Billing, Subscription, and Pricing Plan styles
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Migrate commerce/account-plan screens to the style system without changing pricing, payment, or subscription presentation and behavior.

In scope

  • Adopt tokens, Geist UI typography, shared controls/states, and dialog shells.
  • Move billing, payment, subscription, and pricing-specific layouts/dialog bodies to owning components.
  • Replace Pricing Plan Bootstrap columns/grid and active utilities with feature-owned responsive layout.
  • Remove duplicate overrides and legacy style code after consumer/cascade proof.
  • Preserve currency/price typography unless a documented technical-data case warrants Mono.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No pricing, payment, checkout, plan hierarchy, or responsive redesign.
  • Do not globally generalize feature cards/tables without proven multi-feature reuse.
  • Do not remove Bootstrap globally.

Acceptance criteria

  • Slice styles have clear ownership and no feature dependency on Bootstrap.
  • Pricing columns and payment/subscription dialogs match existing breakpoints and states.
  • Product UI is Geist and ordinary monetary values are not arbitrarily converted to Mono.

Dependencies and order

Depends on shared primitives/shell and follows Settings/Profile/Account.

Verification

  • Review all plan cards, billing tables/forms, payment dialogs, errors, disabled/loading, desktop/mobile, and supported themes.
  • Search Bootstrap and moved/deleted selectors.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the AGENTS.md-required Angular build.

issues.display_title: Issue #1819: [Style System] Migrate Support and Promocodes styles
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Move Support and Promocodes onto the shared foundations while eliminating their feature-level Bootstrap and legacy cascade dependencies.

In scope

  • Capture baselines and map selector consumers.
  • Adopt design tokens, Geist UI typography, shared controls/states, and shared dialog shells.
  • Move feature layouts, tables/cards, fields, feedback states, and dialog bodies to owning components.
  • Replace active Bootstrap utilities/grid/mixins with feature or proven shared CSS.
  • Delete legacy selectors only after consumer and visual verification.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No support workflow, promocode validation, table behavior, or responsive redesign.
  • Feature-only overlays stay component-owned under unique wrappers.
  • Bootstrap remains available to unmigrated slices.

Acceptance criteria

  • Both features follow the style ownership contract and have no feature dependency on Bootstrap.
  • Loading, empty, validation, success, error, and responsive states match baselines.
  • Product UI uses Geist consistently.

Dependencies and order

Depends on shared foundations and follows Billing/Subscription/Pricing.

Verification

  • Search Bootstrap and moved/deleted selectors in the slice.
  • Review forms, lists/tables, feedback states, dialogs, keyboard focus, desktop/mobile, and themes.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the AGENTS.md-required Angular build.

issues.display_title: Issue #1820: [Style System] Migrate authentication flow styles
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Migrate login, signup, password recovery, and related authentication screens without changing their established appearance or behavior.

In scope

  • Adopt tokens, Geist UI typography, shared fields/buttons, validation, loading, disabled, and focus-visible behavior.
  • Move authentication layouts, illustration/content regions, and responsive rules to their owners.
  • Replace active Bootstrap utilities/grid/mixins.
  • Remove obsolete global typography and duplicate component overrides after cascade proof.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No authentication flow, copy, form schema, validation, or responsive redesign.
  • Preserve current asset rendering and error semantics.
  • Do not remove Bootstrap globally.

Acceptance criteria

  • Authentication routes have clear style ownership and no feature-level Bootstrap dependency.
  • All product UI typography is Geist, with no unjustified Mono usage.
  • Current desktop/mobile form composition and states remain compatible.

Dependencies and order

Depends on shared controls/shell and follows Support/Promocodes.

Verification

  • Exercise initial, focus, validation, loading, disabled, success/error, and responsive states.
  • Search for Bootstrap and deleted selectors.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the required Angular build.
  • Compare route baselines.

issues.display_title: Issue #1821: [Style System] Migrate Create Exhibition and shared-dialog styles
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Migrate Create Exhibition and its shared dialog flows while enforcing the repository's PrimeNG dialog ownership contract.

In scope

  • Adopt tokens, Geist UI typography, shared controls/states, and shared dialog chrome.
  • Move wizard/form/layout, cards, media, actions, and feature dialog bodies to owning components.
  • Give every overlay a unique feature wrapper and reuse .v-dialog/mask classes.
  • Replace Bootstrap utilities/grid/mixins used by the feature.
  • Remove dead shared-dialog copies and legacy overrides after consumer proof.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not recreate src/assets/scss/primeNg/_dialog.scss.
  • Keep dialog/_index.scss import-only and feature bodies out of global SCSS.
  • No exhibition creation workflow or visual redesign.

Acceptance criteria

  • Create Exhibition has no feature-level Bootstrap dependency.
  • Reusable dialog shells are global; feature content is local and uniquely scoped.
  • All steps, validation, media states, and responsive layouts match baselines.

Dependencies and order

Depends on shared dialog-shell cleanup and authentication slice.

Verification

  • Search old dialog selectors and Bootstrap consumers.
  • Review every wizard step and open/closed dialog, focus, validation, loading/error, desktop/mobile.
  • Run focused tests and pnpm test:styles.
  • Follow AGENTS.md: use the development build if port 4200 is active; otherwise pnpm build:dev:ssr.

issues.display_title: Issue #1822: [Style System] Migrate public and marketing page styles
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Move Home, About, Catalogue, Contact, and related public layouts to the style system while preserving their current marketing composition.

In scope

  • Capture representative route and breakpoint baselines.
  • Adopt semantic tokens and Geist for product/marketing UI.
  • Keep display typography feature-owned when it intentionally differs from shared product roles.
  • Move page layouts, sections, cards, forms, and responsive rules to owning components.
  • Replace active Bootstrap grid/utilities/mixins and delete proven-dead legacy global page rules.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No brand, copy, content hierarchy, animation, imagery, or marketing redesign.
  • Do not generalize feature cards/sections without demonstrated reuse.
  • Do not remove the Editor content-font catalogue.

Acceptance criteria

  • Public/marketing pages have clear ownership and no feature-level Bootstrap dependency.
  • Navigation, forms, sections, and breakpoints match current baselines.
  • Shared tokens are used where semantically appropriate without flattening intentional display styles.

Dependencies and order

Depends on shared shell and Create Exhibition/shared-dialog work.

Verification

  • Compare all representative routes at desktop/mobile and supported themes.
  • Exercise navigation, forms, hover/focus, loading/error, and responsive states.
  • Search Bootstrap and moved/deleted selectors.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the required Angular build.

issues.display_title: Issue #1823: [Style System] Migrate FAQ, Tutorials, API Tester, maintenance, and model tester styles
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Complete vertical-slice migration for remaining support and internal/legacy pages.

In scope

  • Migrate FAQ, Tutorials, API Tester, maintenance, model tester, and any remaining small routes discovered in the audit.
  • Adopt tokens, Geist/approved Mono usage, shared controls/states, and dialog shells.
  • Keep FAQ card/accordion, API/code data, and tester/maintenance layouts feature-owned.
  • Replace active Bootstrap dependencies.
  • Remove obsolete global page styles and overrides after consumer/cascade verification.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No route behavior, documentation content, testing workflow, or responsive redesign.
  • Mono is limited to code, identifiers, raw API output, and other technical data.
  • Do not promote one-off internal-page styles to global patterns.

Acceptance criteria

  • All included routes follow ownership rules and have no feature-level Bootstrap dependency.
  • Technical typography is intentional and documented.
  • Empty/error/loading, overlay, and responsive states match baselines.

Dependencies and order

Depends on public/marketing migration. This is the final Phase 4 slice before Bootstrap removal.

Verification

  • Inventory routes so no small page is omitted.
  • Search Bootstrap and moved/deleted selectors.
  • Review cards/accordions, code/API output, forms, dialogs, states, desktop/mobile, and themes.
  • Run focused tests, pnpm test:styles, and the AGENTS.md-required Angular build.

issues.display_title: Issue #1824: [Style System] Remove Bootstrap SCSS and compatibility utilities
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Remove Bootstrap as a style dependency once every application slice has an app-owned replacement for the small behavior surface actually used.

In scope

  • Confirm no Bootstrap import, mixin, standard grid consumer, or framework utility dependency remains.
  • Replace the full SCSS import with the proven app-owned button, field, layout, and exact compatibility APIs.
  • Remove Bootstrap-specific Sass configuration, mixins, comments, and temporary paths.
  • Remove bootstrap-scss and its lockfile entry through the package manager.
  • Record CSS bundle/block/size changes against the Phase 0 baseline.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • Do not mass-rename useful app-owned APIs such as .btn or .form-control.
  • Do not recreate Bootstrap's full grid or utility generator.
  • Do not proceed while any active feature depends on Bootstrap behavior.
  • No intentional visual redesign.

Acceptance criteria

  • No Bootstrap imports, Sass mixins, package dependency, or unexplained utility/grid consumers remain.
  • Retained class APIs have complete app-owned base and state behavior.
  • Representative routes and states remain visually compatible.
  • CSS output does not increase without a documented reason.

Dependencies and order

Depends on completion of every Editor and Phase 4 feature migration. This is the Phase 5 removal gate.

Verification

  • Search source and package metadata for Bootstrap imports, mixins, dependencies, grid classes, and utilities.
  • Run pnpm test:styles, focused tests, and the required Angular build.
  • Compare representative desktop/mobile routes, themes, controls, dialogs, and interaction states.
  • Verify the production/development CSS artifact and dependency graph.

issues.display_title: Issue #1825: [Style System] Complete final legacy cleanup and full-app visual verification
issues.main_description_html:
Context and goal

Close the refactor by removing the temporary compatibility layer and verifying the entire application against the original visual contract.

In scope

  • Remove remaining dead selectors, compatibility overrides, legacy product-UI font declarations/faces, and unused vendor/device mixins.
  • Retain all Editor user-content fonts and their styles.
  • Reduce !important, ::ng-deep, raw colors, and ViewEncapsulation.None where the final ownership model makes them unnecessary.
  • Justify/document every remaining exception.
  • Consolidate only utilities and patterns with demonstrated multi-feature reuse.
  • Record final CSS metrics and update style-system documentation/guardrails.

Preservation rules / non-goals

  • No redesign or opportunistic feature work.
  • Do not remove a selector solely because its name looks legacy.
  • Do not remove or consolidate Editor catalogue fonts.
  • Unexplained visual differences must be investigated, not hidden with stronger overrides.

Acceptance criteria

  • src/styles.scss is ordered and import-only; component-imported Sass emits no CSS.
  • Product UI uses Geist and approved technical data uses Geist Mono.
  • Feature styles and PrimeNG dialog bodies have correct owners.
  • Bootstrap and temporary compatibility are absent.
  • Remaining exceptions are minimal, searchable, justified, and documented.
  • Full-app visual and build verification passes.

Dependencies and order

Depends on Bootstrap removal and all preceding implementation issues. This is the final Phase 6 gate.

Verification

  • Run full selector/font/token/encapsulation/dialog ownership audits.
  • Run pnpm test:styles, all relevant focused tests, and the required Angular build.
  • Compare all representative desktop/mobile routes, supported themes, dialogs, and interactive states to the Phase 0 baseline.
  • Confirm Editor content fonts, weights, styles, previews, and rendered output remain unchanged.
